purpose: v3.5's sign gate with MAX_CAP raised 4 -> 12 judge steps; nothing else moves
probe_weights: submission/whitebox_probe (shared trunk, all 3 families, balanced recipe)

selection.method: sweep MAX_CAP in judge steps against both regimes, sign gate retained in every arm
selection.iris_regime: judge blunted to probe_auroc - edge; blunting does not saturate, so the real +0.068 Iris edge is reachable
selection.notus_regime: probe blunted to the measured 0.5586 (and 0.48 inverted), judge left healthy
selection.why_12_not_20_or_40: captures 80% of the probe's edge against cap40's 86%, for a smaller excursion from the only cap regime ever validated on private data; the cap20->cap40 gain is +0.0004 and not worth the extra distance

selection_notes.why_the_v3_5_sweep_missed_this: fit_sign_gate_v3_5.py varied the gate SHAPE at fixed caps of 2 and 4 steps and never raised MAX_CAP. Its 'flat, always open' row removes the direction test at cap 4, which is why it costs -0.0137 on Notus. Keeping the sign gate and raising the ceiling is a different change and was untested.
selection_notes.why_the_first_v3_6_sweep_said_no_effect: test_saturation_v3_6.py built its Iris regime by sharpening the probe, which saturates at ~+0.025 edge. The cap does not bind there, so that arm was uninformative rather than negative.
selection_notes.notus_blind_spot: the local Notus proxy has the judge at 0.938 against real Notus's ~0.864, so the near-zero Notus cost is measured on an easier regime than the one that matters
selection_notes.iris_capture_anomaly: the harness says cap4 should capture 69% on real Iris; the leaderboard says sonic_v3_5 captured 30.5% (0.9444 against judge-alone 0.9236 and probe-alone 0.9918). The cap explains part of the gap. The rest is unexplained, so the projected gain may not land in full.
selection_notes.probe_in_sample_caveat: the probe is in-sample on every dev fold, so absolute levels are inflated; only the comparison across cap values is used
